title: Palantir Called Q2 “Otherworldly.” Monday’s Report Has to Top a $2.18 Billion Consensus
detail:
Palantir Called Q2 “Otherworldly.” Monday’s Report Has to Top a $2.18 Billion Consensus
Rexielyn Diaz
Sat, October 31, 2026 at 6:53 AM CDT 4 min read
PLTR
Trade PLTR on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Palantir Called Q2 "Otherworldly." Monday's Report Has to Top a $2.18 Billion Consensus ©felipecaparros and lmonk72 from pixabay via Canva
Key Takeaways

Palantir fell 6.3% Friday and 7.4% for the week ahead of its November 2 report, closing at $184.

Consensus expects $2.18 billion of third-quarter revenue, above Palantir's own $2.160 billion to $2.164 billion guidance.

Hitting full-year U.S. commercial guidance requires roughly $2.07 billion in the second half, about 22% sequential growth in each quarter.

At 96.8x forward earnings, Monday's report needs a beat and a raise, and U.S. commercial revenue is the number to watch.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) heads into earnings with the toughest setup in software: a premium multiple and a consensus that already sits above its own guidance.

The stock fell 6.3% on Friday to $184 and lost 7.4% for the week as AI spending fears hit tech. It now trades 14% below its 52-week high of $213.

JPMorgan joined the bull camp on Thursday, citing the AI opportunity. Michael Burry is still betting against the stock. Monday's report, due after the close, will test both views.

For a sense of the premium, look at Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ), which reports a day later. Analysts expect AMD's revenue to compound 60.6% a year over the next two years at 45.1x forward earnings, while Palantir's 66.4% comes at 96.8x.

What Monday has to clear

Palantir guided third-quarter revenue to $2.160 billion to $2.164 billion, or 83% growth. Consensus sits higher, at $2.18 billion of revenue and $0.41 of EPS.

That gap is normal here, because Palantir tends to beat its own range. In the second quarter:

Revenue rose 93% to $1.94 billion against a $1.80 billion estimate.

U.S. commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764 million.

Adjusted EPS of $0.41 beat the $0.35 consensus.

Palantir called that quarter "otherworldly" in its release, and it was hard to argue. A similar 7% beat this time would push revenue toward $2.3 billion.

Where has all that left the stock?

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): share price, $ per share, last 1 year (TIKR)

Shares are up 74% from the 52-week low of $106, so expectations have climbed with them.

U.S. commercial carries the guide

Palantir raised full-year revenue guidance to $8.150 billion to $8.158 billion, implying 82% growth. It also guided U.S. commercial revenue above $3.424 billion, at least 134% growth.

By my math, that requires roughly $2.07 billion of U.S. commercial revenue in the second half, or about 22% sequential growth in each of the last two quarters. Second-quarter sequential growth was 28%, so the target looks reachable. That makes the third-quarter U.S. commercial figure more important than the headline.

Bookings support it. Palantir closed a record $2.132 billion of U.S. commercial TCV in the second quarter, up 153%, and U.S. commercial remaining deal value hit $6.24 billion, up 124%.

Here's the split between its two businesses.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): segment revenue, Government vs Commercial, quarterly, $ millions, Q2 2024–Q2 2026 (TIKR)

Commercial now nearly matches government revenue, and it is growing faster.

TIKR tracks 32 analysts on Palantir. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Palantir, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Palantir's Analyst Ratings

Paying 96.8x for the next beat

Palantir trades at 96.8x forward earnings, 157x trailing earnings and 42.6x forward EV to revenue. The Street's $213 average target implies just 15% upside, even after the latest bull calls.

That premium holds only if growth stays near current rates. Guidance already implies growth slowing from 93% in the second quarter to 83% in the third, so any hint of a steeper slowdown would hit the multiple first.

Europe adds a wrinkle. Palantir recently said it cannot shut off NATO's AI system, an effort to calm European worries about depending on U.S. tech.

Put the two multiples next to each other…

Palantir Technologies (PLTR) vs Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): forward (NTM) P/E, last 2 years (TIKR)

Right now, Palantir costs more than twice AMD's multiple for only slightly faster expected growth.

My take: Palantir is executing as well as any software company I follow, and the U.S. commercial bookings make the full-year guide look achievable. But at 96.8x forward earnings, the stock already prices in a beat and raise. I'd wait for a better entry rather than buy ahead of Monday.

The next checkpoint is Monday's report. Watch U.S. commercial revenue against the roughly $930 million it needs to stay on the full-year path, and whether full-year guidance moves above $8.158 billion.

title: Michael Burry Is Still Short Palantir. Here's What Its Nov. 2 Report Has to Show.
detail:
Michael Burry Is Still Short Palantir. Here's What Its Nov. 2 Report Has to Show.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:37 AM CDT 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Michael Burry hasn't backed off his bet against Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR). When the investor of The Big Short fame rolled most of his bearish wagers into two index positions on Oct. 11, he kept his put options on the artificial intelligence (AI) software specialist. These contracts gain value if the stock drops.

Shares haven't cooperated yet. Palantir hit a record close of $209.05 on Oct. 9, and at around $195 as of this writing, it sits only about 7% under that peak.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The company posts its third-quarter results on Monday, Nov. 2, after the market closes.

And I think two numbers from the report matter most to anybody sizing up Burry's bet.

Michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

Burry's bet now stretches into 2027

Burry has been betting against Palantir since the fall of 2025. In April, he wrote that he thinks the company's fundamental value is well below $50 a share.

Later, in a Sept. 28 post, he said he was moving his timeline up. He traded his outright short positions in Palantir and seven other holdings for put options expiring between June and December 2027, arguing that the AI build-out is increasingly funded by debt and might fall apart if spending slows.

Burry has also questioned Palantir's accounting, in a February post arguing that its accounts receivable climbed faster than its revenue in nine of 12 quarters.

But put options expire. For Burry's puts to pay off, Palantir's growth probably has to slow sharply in the coming year or so, and the Nov. 2 report is the next chance to tell if that's starting.

A faster quarter than guided?

Palantir's guidance calls for third-quarter revenue of $2.160 billion to $2.164 billion. Compared to $1.18 billion in the year-ago quarter, that's around 83% growth year over year, slower than 93% growth in the second quarter.

Palantir, however, tends to set its forecasts low. Its second-quarter revenue of $1.94 billion beat the top end of its own forecast by about 7%. In the first quarter of 2026, revenue of $1.63 billion beat the top end by about 6%. And in the fourth quarter of 2025, revenue of $1.41 billion cleared it by about 6% too.

If the third quarter clears its range by a similar margin, revenue could land around $2.3 billion. That would mean growth of about 95%, a little faster than in the second quarter. A result close to $2.16 billion, though, might suggest that growth slowed from the second quarter -- the sort of slowdown Burry's bet needs.

The Q3 results we have already seen from 60% of S&P 500 members through Friday, October 30th, reconfirm the broad-based growth momentum we have become used to in the last few reporting cycles. While the growth pace remains strong, it does not compare favorably with other recent periods, particularly when some of the outlier results are excluded. Most importantly, the revisions trend remains positive, with estimates for 2026 Q4 and full-year 2027 continuing to rise.

We remain in the heart of the Q3 reporting season, with this week bringing in results from more than 1400 companies, including 142 S&P 500 members. This week's busy reporting line-up ranges from Tech bellwethers like Apple, Advanced Micro Devices, Palantir, and others to DuPont, McDonald's, Expedia, and many others. By the end of this week, we will have seen Q3 results from 88% of S&P 500 members.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 300 S&P 500 members that have reported already with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +26.6% from the same period last year on +13.7% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector continues to be a major growth contributor, but the momentum is broad-based, with 15 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track to enjoy positive earnings growth and 9 generating double-digit earnings growth in Q3.

The quarterly chart below details actual results alongside Q3 2026 growth expectations and forward projections.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates, as the chart below shows.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

This positive revisions behavior is not a new development; they extend a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy, following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and also what we saw for Q3, the favorable estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 6 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Industrials, Basic Materials, Finance, and Conglomerates alongside Tech and Energy since the start of October.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates have come down since the start of October for 10 sectors, with the major declines at the Transportation, Autos, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Construction, and Utilities sectors.

Palantir Technologies' (PLTR) business has evolved well beyond its government roots. Once largely associated with public sector contracts, the developer of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered data analytics software has steadily built a presence in commercial markets, where its technology is finding an increasingly receptive audience.

A major force behind this shift is its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), which helps businesses deploy AI agents and put the technology to work across everyday operations.

That growing commercial footprint has not gone unnoticed on Wall Street. JPMorgan analyst Brian Essex recently described Palantir as having "uniquely profitable hyper-growth fundamentals, with potential for substantial disruptive upside within its primary market segments."

He also highlighted the accelerating pace of corporate adoption, as businesses look beyond AI experimentation and demand measurable financial returns from their investments.

The next opportunity to see whether that momentum holds comes on Monday, Nov. 2, when Palantir reports its Q3 FY2026 results after the market closes. After a standout Q2 and a substantial upgrade to its full-year outlook, investors will be watching to see whether the latest numbers can give the stock another reason to climb.

About Palantir Stock

Palantir Technologies develops software platforms for intelligence agencies, defense organizations, and commercial enterprises. With a market cap of approximately $472.9 billion, the company offers four principal products, Gotham, Foundry, Apollo, and Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP), covering everything from data integration and analysis to operational decisions, software deployment, and AI-powered solutions.

Its stock performance has been rather interesting. Shares of the Aventura, Florida-based technology pioneer have slipped 3% over the past 52 weeks. However, the broader picture looks brighter, with PLTR stock gaining 6% year-to-date (YTD) and surging 54% over the latest three-month period.

The rally has not come cheap. Palantir currently trades at 121.91 times forward adjusted earnings and 57.56 times sales, with both valuation multiples comfortably above industry averages.

Palantir Surpasses Q2 Earnings

On Aug. 3, Palantir released its Q2 FY2026 results, reporting strong growth as rising commercial demand for AI lifted revenue and profitability. The performance also prompted management to raise its full-year outlook. Shares gained 2.1% on the announcement day before climbing another 29.5% in the following trading session.

Revenue surged 92.8% year-over-year (YoY) to $1.94 billion, marking the company's strongest reported growth rate to date. The result also topped analysts' expectations of $1.81 billion, reflecting stronger-than-anticipated demand for Palantir's software.

The U.S. business drove much of this expansion, with revenue rising 115% YoY to $1.57 billion. Within the segment, U.S. commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764 million, highlighting growing adoption of Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) among businesses bringing AI into their everyday operations.

Government operations remained another source of strength, with U.S. government revenue increasing 90% from the year-ago period. Commercial demand was equally encouraging, as U.S. commercial total contract value bookings reached $2.13 billion, marking a 153% YoY increase.

Profitability improved alongside revenue growth. Net income attributable to common stockholders climbed 225% from the year-ago period to $1.1 billion. Adjusted EPS came in at $0.41, exceeding Wall Street's estimate of $0.35, while adjusted free cash flow increased 115% YoY to $1.22 billion, representing a 63% margin. The adjusted EPS growth percentage was not specified.

Following the strong quarter, management has raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $8.150 billion–$8.158 billion, implying YoY growth of 82%. U.S. commercial revenue guidance was also increased to more than $3.424 billion, representing expected growth of at least 134%.

The revised outlook also includes adjusted income from operations of $4.889 billion–$4.897 billion and adjusted free cash flow of $4.5 billion–$4.7 billion for FY2026. Meanwhile, for Q3, management expects revenue between $2.160 billion and $2.164 billion, alongside adjusted income from operations of $1.292 billion–$1.296 billion.

Analysts expect earnings growth to remain strong. Q3 FY2026 EPS is projected to increase 83.3% YoY to $0.33. Meanwhile, for FY2026, analysts forecast a 104.7% YoY increase in EPS to $1.29, followed by another 45% rise to $1.87 in FY2027.

What Do Analysts Expect for PLTR Stock?

Among the more bullish voices on Wall Street is JPMorgan's Brian Essex, who has assigned Palantir an "Overweight" rating and established a price target of $262. His stance reflects confidence in the company's ability to capitalize on rising AI adoption and expand its presence across its primary markets.

The broader analyst community is also leaning toward the optimistic side, assigning Palantir an overall rating of "Moderate Buy." Among 31 analysts covering the stock, 22 recommend "Strong Buy," one assigns "Moderate Buy," six recommend "Hold," one has a "Moderate Sell" rating, and one recommends "Strong Sell."

To that end, the average price target of $216.21 implies a potential upside of 15%. Meanwhile, the Street-high target of $265 points to a gain of 41% from current levels.

Options Sentiment Remains Bullish for Palantir Stock

PLTR stock has recently tumbled below its 20-day moving average (MA), indicating bears have taken back control of the near term.

Still, traders are increasingly betting on call options, a setup broadly recognized in the derivatives market as bullish. The put-to-call ratio on contracts expiring Nov. 6 sits at 0.51x as of writing.

According to the latest data from Barchart, the upper price on those options contracts is set at about $214 currently, signaling potential for a more than 10% surge in Palantir through the end of next week.

That said, company executives have predominantly unloaded shares in the trailing six months, which warrants some caution in playing Palantir at current levels.

JPMorgan Initiates PLTR Shares with an 'Overweight' Rating

JPMorgan analyst Brian Essex is confident that Palantir shares are not out of steam just yet. In a research note, Essex assumed coverage of the Nasdaq-listed firm with an "Overweight" rating, saying it has "uniquely profitable hyper-growth fundamentals, with potential for substantial disruptive upside within its primary market segments."

The analyst assigned a $262 price objective to PLTR, indicating potential upside of more than 30% from current levels. He expects the company to benefit as demand for AI Sovereignty continues to grow.

However, the stock is currently trading at 154x earnings, so it's not an inexpensive name to own.

What's the Consensus Rating on Palantir?

While not nearly as bullish as JPM, other Wall Street firms also favor exposure to PLTR shares for the long term.

The consensus rating on Palantir sits at "Moderate Buy," with the mean price target of about $213 indicating potential upside of about 10% from here.
